title.narrative: Early lifesaving Response to Communities Most Vulnerable to El-Nino Induced Riverine Flooding in Luuq, Gedo

description.narrative:
ltpgtVarious projections are in concurrence that there is a greater than 90% chance that El nino will occur and continue through the end of the year, thus affecting 1.2 million people in areas at high risk of flooding. Luuq is one the districts that are highly prone to El nino induced riverine flooding. In line with Reserve Allocation 5, 2023 Strategy, this project focuses on early response, saving lives and reducing the impact of the projected disastrous flooding on communities at the greatest risk. By the time El nino sets in and floods start displacing people, it might be difficult to start planning to respond. Without early action ahead of the rains, many lives, property and livelihoods could be lost and humanitarian needs would rise rapidly.lt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="tab-stops:59.25pt" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="line-height: 107%"gtThe target sites will be the villages and IDP camps that by virtue of their location, are predisposed to riverine flooding induced by El nino. This project will target Luuq Godey, Boyle, Qasale, Bulla Jadid, Hara kowad, Hilac, Dogob, Sariro, Burdubo, Arshame, Lafole, Duyacley, Kahweyne, Qansaxdhere, Daydheere and Al Amin villages/IDP camps. In total, 16,446 people including 2,796 women, 5,427 girls, 2,631 men and 5,592 boys will be targeted. These are from 2741 households. Each HH will receive one standard NFI kit and two plastic sheets.lt/spangtltspan style="line-height: 107%"gt NFI kits will help the families to safely handle water, prepare food, cook and serve in hygienic conditions that will minimize the spread of cholera and water-borne diseases. The blankets will protect the vulnerable from extreme colds while mosquito nets will prevent the spread of malaria whose conditions are perfected by anticipated conditions of stagnant water around the sites. Plastic sheets on the other hand will help the affected households to repair and improve the capacity of shelters to protect families especially young boys and girls, women, elderly and people living with disability from rain, wind and extreme cold.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="Default"gtThis project is part of a wider integrated response featuring Shelter/NFIs, Food Security, WASH and health initiatives in Luuq district. While HAPEN will implement SNFIs component, Himilo Organizaton for Development (HOD) will address food security as Active in Development Aid (ADA) provide WASH and health services. HAPEN will closely coordinate with these partners in order to approach the effects of flooding from a multi-sectoral perspective and amplify the benefits of complementarity. HAPEN will also actively look out for other partners working in the district in order to strengthen coordination. The local administration will play a catalytic role in these coordination arrangements.lt/pgtltp class="" style=""gt The primary beneficiaries will be those that lack basic NFIs and whose shelters are least prepared to protect the families in the likely event of El nino-induced riverine foods. The vulnerability criteria will still apply, including households with pregnant and lactating mothers, elderly, people living with disabilities (PLWDs, child-head households, women-headed HHs and those with a high number of children under 5 years.lt/pgtltp class="Default"gtA standard community response and feedback mechanism (CRFM) will be established to facilitate gathering of feedback and complaints from the affected population. It will include a CRFM desk and a toll free number to act as a hotline. Protection will be mainstreamed throughout the implementation period to ensure the principle of Do no harm is upheld. ltbrgtltbrgt Once distribution is completed, a post distribution monitoring will be conducted to determine how effective the distribution was by focusing on quantity and quality of items, participation, distribution process, usefulness to the beneficiaries, protection considerations during the implementation and impact among others. The PDM will utilize the Shelter Cluster PDM tools. The use of these tools which will target a reasonable sample of the beneficiaries to ensure reliability of data and will be closely coordinated with the Shelter Cluster.lt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gtltbrgtlt/pgt
